A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same telephone-game study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original transmission-chain experiments with five LLMs, three tasks, and 20 initial texts, including statistical analyses, attractor estimates, and generated-text examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments with six principal LLMs and additional robustness, temperature, Base/Instruct, and heterogeneous-chain comparisons.

M1.justification: The iterative text-passing framework and linear-regression attractor estimator remain unchanged in Section 3. Added models, mixed populations, temperatures, and prompts are experimental conditions within that framework. Revised numerical estimates do not establish an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: The scientific-abstract, news, and social-media sources and three principal tasks are retained. v2 adds heterogeneous Llama3-8B/Mistral-7B transmission scenarios and graded requirements for modifying texts (B.2.3–B.2.4). The 100-text replication increases sampling within existing data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 retains the five original principal models and adds GPT-4o-mini to their comparisons. Figure 5b additionally compares Base and Instruct versions of Llama3-70B and Mixtral-8x7B, extending the existing model families.

E3.justification: The principal 50-generation design persists, but v2 adds a 100-initial-text replication, five paraphrases per task, graded modification constraints, temperature sweeps, Base/Instruct conditions, and two starting orders for heterogeneous chains. It also removes the embedding-based cosine-similarity evaluation described in v1 Section 3.2.

E4.justification: v2 adds sample-size and prompt robustness tests, a direct control for task constraints, and temperature, fine-tuning, and heterogeneous-chain analyses (Figure 5; Figures S3–S6). The semantic-convergence analysis in v1 Section 4.4/Figure 7 is removed. The collapse case study and 10-to-50-generation attractor validation are retained.

E5.justification: v1 displays posterior-difference means and significance stars; v2 reports explicit 95% credible-interval endpoints in Tables 2–12. v2 also adds error bars to the principal attractor estimates and reports variability across prompt paraphrases. Both versions retain five seeds for the principal experiments; no increase is stated.

E6.justification: Beyond new model and control results, retained-model estimates change: Mixtral-8x7B's Rephrase toxicity-attractor strength is approximately 0.45 in v1 Figure 6 and 0.90 in v2 Figure 4. The revised Bayesian analysis no longer supports the between-model toxicity-position differences reported in v1 Figure 10; v2 Table 5 intervals all include zero. Semantic-convergence results are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 retains the linear recurrence, convergence condition |s| < 1, position I/(1-s), and strength 1-s. Generalizing the generation-count notation adds no substantive theory. The Bayesian model definitions are also retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Although the abstract's central message is retained, v2 reframes the contributions around deficiencies in single-turn evaluation and adds headline claims about temperature and fine-tuning effects. Its discussion extends the implications to training and alignment. The earlier contribution concerning between-chain semantic convergence is dropped.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking temperature to relaxed constraints and Base/Instruct differences to data curation and human preferences. It discusses the length exception in the constraint experiment and makes stronger alignment implications. v1's explicit warning that fitted fixed points do not prove attractor existence is omitted; B.3.1 additionally introduces a rationale for interpreting uncorrected KS-test trends.

D1.justification: v2 supplies exact paraphrased and graded-constraint prompts, adds environmental resource estimates, and explicitly identifies the repository as another source of generated data. Core decoding parameters, hardware descriptions, hashtag filtering, and existing code/data URLs remain. These are documentation additions rather than evidence that the original settings changed.

R1.justification: Related work expands with dedicated discussions of Bayesian Iterated Learning and social-context evaluation, including Ren et al., Zhu and Griffiths, Zhou et al., and Huang et al. v2 substantively distinguishes its fixed-point approach from convergence-to-priors accounts and clarifies its cultural-evolution positioning. These changes exceed citation-style or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the contribution list and discussion, expands the explanation of culture, compresses the methods and qualitative-results narrative, and removes Section 4.4. Appendix B gains a detailed subsection structure, while reproducibility and ethics statements are added. These constitute substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: v2 rearranges and substantially compresses the distribution and KS plots, moves the attractor-method illustration to Figure S1, and adds Figure 5 and Figures S3–S6. Posterior heatmaps become interval tables, attractor plots gain error bars, and the semantic-convergence figure disappears. Legends and appendix plots are updated for GPT-4o-mini.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence: its direct manipulation of allowable text changes addresses confounding in v1's comparison of different tasks, while larger-sample and prompt-paraphrase checks test previously unexamined robustness (B.2). Temperature and Base/Instruct comparisons replace some speculation with empirical evidence, and explicit credible intervals improve scrutiny. These gains outweigh the loss of semantic-convergence analysis and less cautious claims about attractors and alignment.
